exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Director, Cathay two five one, heading zero four zero, descending to three thousand feet.
exchanges.meaning: Initial approach check-in: reporting current heading and descent to the Director controller.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, Hong Kong Director, turn left heading wun zero zero, intercept localizer Runway zero sev-en left, report established.
exchanges.meaning: Radar vector to intercept the ILS localizer for Runway 07L, with the mandatory report-established requirement.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Turn left heading wun zero zero, intercept localizer Runway zero sev-en left, report established, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Full readback of the intercept vector confirming the heading, runway and reporting requirement.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, confirm localizer established.
exchanges.meaning: Controller's confirmation query verifying localizer capture before the frequency transfer.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Hong Kong Director, Cathay two five one, established localizer Runway zero sev-en left.
exchanges.meaning: The mandatory "established" report that signals Director to transfer the flight to Tower for landing clearance.

exchanges.speaker: ATC
exchanges.text: Cathay two five one, roger, contact Hong Kong Tower wun wun eight day-see-mal sev-en.
exchanges.meaning: Handoff to Tower frequency 118.7 once localizer establishment is confirmed.

exchanges.speaker: Pilot
exchanges.text: Tower wun wun eight day-see-mal sev-en, Cathay two five one.
exchanges.meaning: Brief readback of the frequency transfer to Tower.

vocabulary.definition: VHF navigation transmitter (108.10–111.95 MHz) at the departure end of the runway; radiates 90 Hz modulation on the left and 150 Hz on the right — the signals are equal when the aircraft is aligned with the runway centerline.
ATC heading vector assigned to capture the final approach course, e.g. "Turn left heading 100, intercept localizer 07L".
Mandatory instruction to notify ATC upon localizer capture; the established report triggers handoff to Tower.
Pilot confirmation that the CDI needle is centered within half-scale deflection — the mandatory check-in phraseology.
Extremely narrow course: ±2.5° full-scale CDI deflection, roughly 700 ft wide at the threshold.
Spurious ground reflections radiated outside the main beam (±35°); avoided by intercepting at under 30°.
On localizer intercept the pilot presses the LOC or APP pushbutton; the autopilot transitions from HDG mode to LOC* (Capture) then LOC (Track) as the localizer diamond moves inward on the PFD.

quiz.question: When an aircraft is tracking inbound on the ILS localizer course, what angular displacement does full-scale deflection of the Course Deviation Indicator (CDI) needle represent?
quiz.explanation: A standard VOR CDI needle represents 10° for full-scale deflection, but an ILS localizer is four times more sensitive: full-scale deflection represents approximately 2.5° off the centerline.

quiz.question: What is the primary operational objective of the ATC instruction "Report established on localizer"?
options: To confirm the aircraft has captured the final approach course and can be safely transferred to the Tower controller for landing sequence.
To authorize the flight to begin immediate descent below minimum vectoring altitude.
To cancel all wake turbulence separation minimums.
To verify the aircraft's fuel reserve.
quiz.explanation: Under ICAO Doc 4444, when the aircraft reports established on the localizer, approach radar control confirms lateral guidance has succeeded and transfers control to the Tower for landing clearance.

sections.heading: Section 2: Core Learning Content & Vocabulary Table
sections.body:
| Phrase / Command | ICAO Standard Definition | Phonetic Guide | Operational Example |
|---|---|
| Turn to intercept localizer | Heading vector assigned to capture final approach course. | turn to in-ter-SEPT LOH-ka-ly-zer | "Turn left heading 100, intercept localizer 07L." |
| Report established | Mandatory instruction to notify ATC upon localizer capture. | re-PORT es-TAB-lisht | Triggers handoff to Tower. |
| Established on localizer | Pilot confirmation that CDI needle is centered within half-scale. | es-TAB-lisht on LOH-ka-ly-zer | Mandatory check-in phraseology. |
| Localizer beam width | Extremely narrow course: ±2.5° full scale deflection. | LOH-ka-ly-zer beem | Approx. 700 ft wide at threshold. |
| False course / False lobes | Spurious ground reflections radiated outside main beam (±35°). | fawls korss | Avoided by intercepting under 30°. |

sections.heading: Section 8: Spaced Repetition Review Drill
sections.body:
- Day 30 Review (+1d): Standard speed gate on intermediate final approach is 160 knots to 4 DME. Approach must be fully stabilized by 1,000 ft in IMC.
- Day 1 Review (+30d Milestone): The 30-Day forgetting curve benchmark! Complete review of ICAO numbers (WUN, TREE, FOW-ER, FIFE, NIN-ER, DAY-SEE-MAL) and phonetic alphabet clarity under heavy static.

sections.heading: Section 9: Fun Aviation Fact — Jimmy Doolittle's 1929 Blind Flight
sections.body: On September 24, 1929, aviation pioneer Jimmy Doolittle took off, flew a 15-mile course, and landed a biplane without ever seeing outside! His cockpit was completely sealed in canvas. Doolittle navigated and landed relying purely on an artificial horizon, directional gyro, and a primitive visual radio localizer — inventing instrument flight and the foundation of the modern ILS!
